rationale: The Yes/No options only make sense with the question 'Do you already have a personal user account?', which is an h4 not tied to the radios by a fieldset/legend or named group.
The outline is h1 followed directly by this h4 in the same page flow, with no h2 or h3 between them, so two levels are skipped.

The checkboxes answer one question ('Which types of waste do you transport regularly?') shown only as an h4, not tied to the options by a named group; the labels alone omit the 'transport regularly' context.
The page's h1 is followed directly by this h4 with no intervening h2/h3 in the same content flow, leaving a gap in the outline.
The joined name 'Date of issue Day' reads naturally as a group label plus the field's own label, clearly saying what to enter.
The table holds data (names, ages, birthdays) and its label row uses td instead of th, so no cell is marked as a header.
The empty th is the top-left corner cell over row headers (Jackie, Beth); it heads no data cells.
The h3 directly follows the page h1 with no h2 in between, and both are in the same main content flow, so a level is skipped.
The h5 follows the h3 in the same main section with no h4 between them, skipping a level.
The named table is the outer 800px page frame holding border images, banner, navigation and content blocks; it only lays out content (role LayoutTable).
The named table is the outer page frame with border images and nested layout tables; it lays out the page rather than presenting data.
The named table is the outer page layout frame (borders, banner, nav, content); the nested price table is a separate element, so this table is layout.
The table pairs band names in the top row with concert dates below, a data table whose label row uses td, not th.
The th sits alone in a one-cell table used as a section headline image and heads no data cells; its missing alt text is an image problem rather than a header problem.
The radios have no accessible names at all and the question 'Which is your favorite city park?' is only shown in a nearby cell, not tied to them by a named group.
The radios have empty accessible names, and the 'Name:' prompt with Mr./Mrs. is only plain text near them, not a group name or labels.
The named table is the outer page layout frame (borders, banner, nav, content); the nested survey results table is a separate element.
This small table only positions radio buttons next to spacer images; it holds no data needing headers.
This table only lays out option labels (None, Central Park, Grand Park) beside spacer images to align with the radios; it presents no data needing headers.
The table only aligns three radio buttons next to spacer images; it presents no data with labels, so it is a layout table.
The table only places option labels (Jurassic Park, South Park, Other) beside spacer images to align with radio buttons; it is layout, not data needing headers.
The table lays out form fields and their text labels side by side with spacer images; it is a layout table for a form, not tabular data.
The block holds the site logo and a quick topic menu at the top of the page, so it is the page header, and the landmarks list is empty, so there is no banner landmark.
The block is the site's main menu (Home, News, Tickets, Survey) and the page exposes no landmarks, so it is not a navigation landmark.
The element is an in-content h2 'Elsewhere on the Web' with class 'header'; it is a section heading, not the page header.
The block sits at the bottom of the demo page with copyright and legal links, so it is the page footer, and no contentinfo landmark exists.
